solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finish off Chablis just opened during meal

indicators.note: something just opened shows only its very beginning, so only the initial letter is used
one thing happening during another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
the opening letter of the wine's name

explanation.surface: A diner polishes off a bottle of Chablis that was opened only during the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' looks like drinking up the wine, but it is the definition: to scupper a plan is to wreck it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper something is to ruin or destroy it, originally by sinking a ship, so it means to finish off.

clue.text: Heavy coffins destabilised a cargo ship

indicators.note: a thing destabilised is upset and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Heavy coffins in the hold capsize a cargo ship.
explanation.definitionFit: These are ancient stone coffins, often massive and carved, the plural of a Greek-derived word.

clue.text: Leaders of unions now conduct urgent talks in full

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their front, so each word gives its initial

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Trade union leaders now hold urgent talks in full session.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut film or text is complete, shown with nothing removed.

clue.text: Show off, broadcast succeeded

blocks.note: to put a programme on air is to broadcast it
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A show-off went on the airwaves and was a success.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on airs is an idiom for behaving pretentiously, affecting superiority.

clue.text: Centre redeveloped to be modern

indicators.note: a site redeveloped is rebuilt in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A town centre is rebuilt so as to look up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent belongs to the near past or present, hence new and up to date.

clue.text: Our side at PT showed distress

blocks.note: our side is us, or we
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our team became upset during a PT (physical training) session at school.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the old British name for school gym lessons; here it is simply two letters taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wept shed tears, an outward display of sadness or distress.

clue.text: Humour with appeal

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with; the word also starts with the answer's letters, a coincidence
it is slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Humour that has charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is clever verbal humour, the quickness that makes people laugh.

clue.text: Foretell the closure of Dover?

blocks.note: Dover is a port, an example signalled by the question mark
a closure is an end

explanation.surface: Someone predicts that Dover will be shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is England's main Channel ferry port, and a 'port end' is a closure of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signal in advance that something will happen, to presage or foretell it.

clue.text: Fabulous bird's music heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: rock is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: Someone hears the song of a legendary bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian legend, as in Sinbad's voyages, so it belongs to fable.

clue.text: Returning pet I go with few words

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a cat is a common pet
taken as written
a go in a game is your turn

explanation.surface: Someone coming back from walking a pet says very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative, saying little in conversation.

clue.text: Shakespeare, say: fun, perfect for audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so this word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: play is fun and games
right means correct or perfect

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's work: entertaining and just right for theatregoers.
explanation.walkthrough: A wright is a maker, as in shipwright, so the sound of 'right' is spelt that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is the best-known example of a dramatist, a writer of stage works.

clue.text: Regularly one is moved to take in paper

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted out of their order into a new arrangement
to take something in is to absorb it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the three letters of the word rearranged
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A person is regularly moved to take in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the Financial Times, is a London newspaper printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done often happens frequently, which is what regularly means in loose usage.

clue.text: Lead implicitly offered by Roosevelt?

blocks.note: surface reading: the political leadership a president offered his country
setter's reading: the word lead dealt afresh gives the answer's letters, so the phrase implies its own rearrangement

explanation.surface: Franklin Roosevelt offered the nation leadership without spelling it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of 'Lead' given a fresh deal spell DEAL, a new deal of LEAD, which is also FDR's 1930s programme of economic recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's 1930s programme of reforms to pull America out of the Depression was famously named this way.

clue.text: Aggressive type passionate against Germany

blocks.note: warm feelings are ardent or passionate
leaning against something is leaning on it
GER is an abbreviation for Germany

explanation.surface: A belligerent person feels strongly opposed to Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger stirs up or advocates war, the epitome of an aggressive person.

clue.text: Scottish dish is given to witch: good

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old woman or witch
G is a standard abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witch is served a Scottish dish and pronounces it good.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' does double work in the surface but supplies its own letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis, sheep's offal cooked in a stomach casing, is the national dish of Scotland.

clue.text: Aisle? Clear a path!

blocks.note: first meaning: a passage between rows of seats
second meaning: a shout telling people to move aside

explanation.walkthrough: The noun is the British word for an aisle in a theatre or bus; shouted, it orders a crowd to make way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a passageway between seats and is also called out to demand that people let you through.

clue.text: Sat at length after this?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone sat for a long time following some event
setter's reading: Sat is the abbreviation of a weekday, and written in full it follows the answer

explanation.surface: Someone stayed seated for a long time after some ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' is not a verb but the short form of Saturday; 'at length' means spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: In the week Saturday comes straight after it, so it is the day that Saturday follows.

clue.text: Demanding, like ruler

blocks.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone is as imperious as a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking means requesting or requiring, as in asking a lot, the sense of demanding.

clue.text: Disturbed, seeing end of libellous book

indicators.note: things disturbed are knocked out of place, so the letters are jumbled
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is upset on reading the end of a libellous book.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'book' looks like the libellous one; it is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible, telling of the Creation.

clue.text: Swimmer over the top, I hesitate to say

blocks.note: OTT is the common abbreviation for over the top, excessive
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A swimmer is going too far, and the speaker hesitates to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is an aquatic mammal, an expert swimmer of rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Instructed, we hear, to get sweet cake

indicators.note: what we hear is taken by its sound alone

blocks.note: instructed means taught

explanation.surface: Someone is taught how to bake a sweet cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, in which the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of central European origin, typically a dessert.

clue.text: Wife in the stand looking very warm

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so it goes within the longer word

blocks.note: a stand at a sports ground is its tiered seating
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife up in the stand at a match looks hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sweating is perspiring, the visible sign of being very hot.

clue.text: With energy, answer back

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone retorts with spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer back' looks like a phrase, to retort; 'back' is the definition, in the sense of past time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago and back both refer to time past, as in years ago or years back.

clue.text: Scrap boisterous practical joke

blocks.note: first meaning: a torn piece of cloth
second meaning: a rowdy prank, as played by students

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a rowdy prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb, to cancel; it is a noun, a fragment of fabric. In Britain a student rag is also a charity week of stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a remnant of cloth and, chiefly in Britain, a noisy prank or stunt.

clue.text: Literal contribution to party politics

indicators.note: a contribution to something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A literal-minded contribution is made to party politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' looks like an adjective; printers use it as a noun for a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing a literal is a mistake of a single letter, which is exactly a typing error.

clue.text: Man concealing weapon in jacket, for example

indicators.note: something concealing another hides it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A man hides a gun inside his jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'jacket' seems to be where the weapon is hidden; it is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one instance of an item of clothing, so the general term is defined by example.
